sentences.text: Anne Rice -LRB- born Howard Allen Frances O'Brien ; October 4 , 1941 -RRB- is an American author of gothic fiction , Christian literature , and erotica .	gothic fiction	gothic fiction	Christian literature	Christian literature	erotica	erotica

She is perhaps best known for her popular and influential series of novels , The Vampire Chronicles , revolving around the central character of Lestat .	The Vampire Chronicles	The Vampire Chronicles	Lestat	Lestat de Lioncourt

Books from The Vampire Chronicles were the subject of two film adaptations , Interview with the Vampire in 1994 , and Queen of the Damned in 2002 .	The Vampire Chronicles	The Vampire Chronicles	Interview with the Vampire	Interview with the Vampire (film)	Queen of the Damned	Queen of the Damned (film)
Born in New Orleans , Rice spent much of her early life there before moving to Texas , and later to San Francisco .	New Orleans	New Orleans	San Francisco	San Francisco
She was raised in an observant Catholic family , but became an agnostic as a young adult .	Catholic	Catholic Church	agnostic	agnostic

She began her professional writing career with the publication of Interview with the Vampire in 1976 , while living in California , and began writing sequels to the novel in the 1980s .	Interview with the Vampire	Interview with the Vampire (film)

In the mid-2000s , following a publicized return to Catholicism , Rice published the novels Christ the Lord : Out of Egypt and Christ the Lord : The Road to Cana , fictionalized accounts of certain incidents in the life of Jesus .	Jesus	Jesus

Several years later she distanced herself from organized Christianity , citing disagreement with the Church 's stances on social issues but pledging that faith in God remained `` central to -LSB- her -RSB- life . ''
However , she now considers herself a secular humanist .	secular humanist	secular humanist
Rice 's books have sold nearly 100 million copies , placing her among the most popular authors in recent American history .
While reaction to her early works was initially mixed , she became more popular with critics and readers in the 1980s .
Her writing style and the literary content of her works have been deeply analyzed by literary commentators .
She was married to poet and painter Stan Rice for 41 years , from 1961 until his death from brain cancer in 2002 at age 60 .	Stan Rice	Stan Rice
She and Stan had two children , Michele , who died of leukemia at age five , and Christopher , who is also an author .	leukemia	leukemia	Christopher	Christopher Rice

In addition to her vampire novels , Rice has authored books such as The Feast of All Saints -LRB- adapted for television in 2001 -RRB- and Servant of the Bones , which formed the basis of a 2011 comic book miniseries .	The Feast of All Saints	The Feast of All Saints (novel)	Servant of the Bones	Servant of the Bones	comic book	comic book
Several books from The Vampire Chronicles have been adapted as comics by various publishers .	The Vampire Chronicles	The Vampire Chronicles

Rice has also authored erotic fiction under the pen names Anne Rampling and A. N. Roquelaure , including Exit to Eden , which was later adapted into a 1994 film .	Exit to Eden	Exit to Eden	1994 film	Exit to Eden (film)
